newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port workers to strike over U.S. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Japan port workers to strike over U.S. sanctions.

text.p: Japanese port workers will stage a 24-hour nationwide strike next week to protest against a U.S. decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports, union officials said on Wednesday.
The planned strike is also to seek shorter working hours and job security for the port workers, the officials said.

Two major labour unions -- the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions and the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions -- have decided to stage a 24-hour strike from the morning of March 12.
Workers from the two unions will also refuse to handle cargoes on Sundays from March 16 onwards, they said.
The strike would affect operations of container ships docking at all major ports in Japan, including Yokohama and Kobe, an official of the National Council of Dock Workers' Unions said.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory practices at Japanese ports, said last week it would slap $100,000 surcharges from April 14 on vessels of Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK every time they stop at a U.S. port.
"The FMC's claim is totally unacceptable to us," said an official of the Japan Confederation of Port and Transport Workers' Unions.
